headline: Chinese researchers found that an AI system reading whole breast ultrasound videos helped less experienced specialists diagnose suspicious lesions far more accurately.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered to 4: the publisher headline says the AI reads 'better than doctors', but it beat junior and attending readers only, not senior ones, and was tested only on already-suspicious hospital cases.
importance_line: Women facing a possible breast cancer diagnosis could get more accurate readings where senior specialists are scarce, but experienced readers gained little and use in screening is unproven.
summary: Scienmag reports on a prospective study across four Chinese hospitals, published in Holistic Integrative Oncology, in which an AI system called TGMIL that analyses whole ultrasound video clips rather than single frames raised junior sonographers' (ultrasound specialists') accuracy on suspicious breast lesions from 66.7 to 89.2 percent and attending-level sonographers' from 80.8 to 90.0 percent. Senior sonographers, who already scored highest, gained no significant benefit and the AI alone scored below them, and the authors say it needs testing in screening populations before wider use.
notes: Text read on the Bioengineer.org copy, which credits Scienmag as the news source; the link points to the Scienmag original (its page title and canonical link were checked, its text was not read separately). The date of the underlying study is not stated.
